UFO expert Mark Rodeghier reportedly revealed the reason behind the Air Force's alleged involvement in obstructing the UAP probe during an interview with Ross Coulthart in Reality Check. The expert revealed that the issue likely dated back to the Cold War era and said that the authorities wanted to keep the development of secret aircraft hidden from public scrutiny. Mark stated:

"I suppose it goes back to the Cold War, and this goes up to the Robertson Panel, and, the way in general, the defense, military, and intelligence agencies, and the CIA, have treated not just the UFO subjects, but things like what MK-ULTRA and so forth."

Mark added that the Robertson Panel should be considered while addressing the issue. He said that the issue stemmed back to the way the military, intelligence agencies, and the CIA handled sensitive subjects like unidentified flying objects and programs like MK-ULTRA.

Continue reading more about the story.

Mark Rodeghier explained why the Air Force was accused of blocking the UAP investigation

In Reality Check, Mark Rodeghier explained that critics accused the Air Force of blocking serious UAP investigations for several reasons. He mentioned that the problem started in the Cold War era, when military and intelligence agencies and the CIA routinely kept large amounts of information secret.

According to him, this culture of secrecy extended to UFO reports, while officials were often reluctant to share information that the public believed it had a right to know.

He argued that authorities viewed the topic of unidentified flying objects as a possible challenge to their power and credibility. In his view, the concern was not necessarily about extraterrestrial life but about the public, who might lose trust in official statements if people discover that important information had been withheld.

Mark also claimed that Project Blue Book largely functioned as a public relations effort after 1953. As a result, it led many critics to believe that misinformation had been used to downplay unexplained sightings. Mark mentioned,

"There is nothing in UFO. After all, the Blue Book was essentially a propaganda campaign after 1953. So, disinformation took place."

He added that another reason for dismissing UFO reports was to protect classified aircraft programs. Officials could divert attention away from secret military aviation projects by encouraging people to dismiss unusual 'unidentified flying object' sightings as mundane phenomena. Ultimately, Mark mentioned that these factors fueled accusations that the Air Force obstructed meaningful UAP investigations.

Mark Rodeghier said the Air Force should have taken UFO reports more seriously

According to Mark, one of the main reasons the U.S. Air Force played down the issue related to unidentified flying objects after the Robertson Panel was to make it seem less important. He explained that officials believed that a large number of UFO reports could overwhelm reporting systems and make it harder to identify genuine incursions by possible foreign adversaries into the U.S. airspace. Mark said,

"I think one of the main excuses used for attempts by the US Air Force after the Robertson Commission was essentially to reduce the significance of the UFO problem."

Mark believed that the Air Force's job was to protect the U.S. airspace from any intrusion. He argued that it should not have mattered whether the object was a strange creature arriving in a flying saucer or a Russian bomber because any unidentified entry into American airspace deserved attention and investigation. In his perspective, the Air Force should have learned about such incidents and acted accordingly.
